parts.text:
Copper(II) sulfate crystals are made by the reaction between copper(II) carbonate and dilute
sulfuric acid, using the following steps.
The sulfuric acid has a concentration of 0.100 mol / dm .
step 1 Powdered copper(II) carbonate is added to dilute sulfuric acid. The mixture is
stirred. A reaction occurs.
step 2 More copper(II) carbonate is added, with stirring, until the reaction stops.
step 3 Unreacted copper(II) carbonate is separated from aqueous copper(II) sulfate by
filtration.
step 4 Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is heated until some of the water evaporates.
step 5 The remaining solution is allowed to cool and crystallise.
step 6 The crystals are removed and dried.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Give two observations in step 1.

parts.label: (ii)

that will dissolve at that temperature.
